claims: Peptides are short chains of 2–100 amino acids.
Peptides act as signaling molecules in the body.
Popular types of peptides include GLP-1 agonists, collagen peptides, and BPC-157.
Many popular "research" peptides lack FDA approval.
GLP-1 agonists like Ozempic are used in prescription medications for type 2 diabetes.
Peptides are used in prescription medications for osteoporosis.
Peptides are used in prescription medications for growth hormone deficiencies.
Copper peptides are used in creams and serums.
BPC-157 and TB-500 are used for muscle growth, fat loss, and tissue repair.
Collagen peptides are common nutritional supplements for skin and joint health.
Signaling peptides trigger skin to produce more collagen.
Carrier peptides deliver trace elements like copper to aid wound healing.
Neurotransmitter peptides block chemicals that cause muscle contraction to reduce wrinkles.
Sermorelin and Ipamorelin are hormone replacement peptides.
Bioactive food-derived peptides are found in protein sources like whey, casein, and soy.
BPC-157 and CJC-1295 are sold as "research chemicals".
BPC-157 and CJC-1295 lack FDA, safety, or efficacy testing.
